annotations.title: Measure a category against its usual month

description:
Measure ONE spending category for one month against its usual month: the month total, the usual amount, and the difference. It draws no card.

Call it when the person asks how much they spent on one category in a month, or how a month compares to usual ("how much did I spend on groceries this month compared to usual?"). For several categories at once, or for a total by category, use `well_sum_transactions` instead.

**"Usual" is the mean of the 3 full months before the month.** A month with no row of the category counts 0. Read `baseline_complete` before you call the figure usual: when it is false, some of those months had no transaction in scope at all, so say which months had data (`baseline_activity`) and do not call the mean usual.

The month defaults to the running month in UTC. The running month is partial: `month_complete` is false, so say the month is not over. A month after the running month is refused.

Figures are per currency, with no conversion: one entry in `currencies` per currency, at most 10. Never add two currencies together. An empty `currencies` means the category has no row in the whole window. A month amount is the net of the category's money in and money out, as a magnitude: spend minus refunds on a feed that keeps one sign convention. When a large share of the category's rows over the window is negative and a large share is positive, the workspace pools a feed that signs its outflows with one that stores magnitudes, and no single spend figure exists: the call refuses with `refusal_reason: "mixed_sign_conventions"` and the two row counts, and measures nothing.

`uncategorized_in_month.count` is the rows of the month with no category at all; a row filed under a category the person typed is not counted. Some of them can belong to this category, so the month total is a floor when the count is not 0: say so. `excluded_malformed` counts the rows with an amount that could not be read.

**The category list depends on the workspace.** A personal space files household categories, a company workspace business categories, and both file the shared ones. A category outside the workspace's list returns `refusal_reason` and `allowed_categories`, and nothing is measured. A personal space shows some shared keys under its own name: TRAVEL_TRANSPORT ("Transport & travel"), MEALS_ENTERTAINMENT ("Restaurants & bars"), BANK_FX_PAYMENT_PROCESSING_FEES ("Bank fees"), TREASURY_PLACEMENT_OUT ("Savings & investments (out)"), TREASURY_REDEMPTION_IN ("Savings & investments (in)"), INVESTMENT_INTEREST_INCOME ("Interest"), LOAN_DRAWDOWNS_REPAYMENTS ("Loans & credit"), INTER_ACCOUNT_TRANSFER_SAME_ENTITY ("Transfers between my accounts"), FX_CONVERSION_PRINCIPAL ("Currency exchange"), UNCATEGORISED_SUSPENSE ("Uncategorised"). Name a category with `category.label` or `category.names` from the result, never with the key.

`scope` defaults to `own`: the workspace's own transactions. `own_and_adopted` adds the rows a parent workspace shared with it.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no other tool call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

category.description: The catalog key of ONE category. A personal space names some shared keys differently: TRAVEL_TRANSPORT ("Transport & travel"), MEALS_ENTERTAINMENT ("Restaurants & bars"), BANK_FX_PAYMENT_PROCESSING_FEES ("Bank fees"), TREASURY_PLACEMENT_OUT ("Savings & investments (out)"), TREASURY_REDEMPTION_IN ("Savings & investments (in)"), INVESTMENT_INTEREST_INCOME ("Interest"), LOAN_DRAWDOWNS_REPAYMENTS ("Loans & credit"), INTER_ACCOUNT_TRANSFER_SAME_ENTITY ("Transfers between my accounts"), FX_CONVERSION_PRINCIPAL ("Currency exchange"), UNCATEGORISED_SUSPENSE ("Uncategorised").

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

month.description: The month to measure, `YYYY-MM`. Omit for the running month in UTC. A later month is refused.

scope.description: `own` (the default) for the workspace's own rows, `own_and_adopted` to add the rows a parent shared.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_measure_category_trend

allowed_categories.description: With refusal_reason: the categories this workspace files and is offered. Send `label` back; `name` is how the workspace shows it.

label.description: The category's label in this workspace.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. Start the reply with one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.
